newsitem.title: UK: Stocks hit record in London, rise in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Stocks hit record in London, rise in Tokyo.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - London's FTSE 100 share index rose to a record high close, but fell short of its all-time intraday high as a dithering Dow took the steam out of a strong early rally in British blue-chips. The FTSE closed 50.6 points higher at 4,357.7, just beating the previous closing high set Feb. 19.

FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX index of top shares closed at a record high, pushed upwards by the strong dollar and rally in the auto sector following bullish comments from a Daimler official on 1996, 1997 results. The DAX-30 index of leading shares closed up 56.80 points at 3,320.66, a record. In post-bourse trade the index was up 86.35 at 3,345.09.

PARIS - French shares staged a strong rally, helped by the dollar and bullish underlying sentiment, and closed a whisper away from their all-time high reached Feb. 18 of this year. The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended up 51.43 points, or 1.98 percent, at 2,651.69.

ZURICH - Swiss shares firmed more than 1 percent to end slightly below the day's highs, regaining the 4,500-point level in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) after a three-day fall. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended up 32.45 points, or 1.05 percent, to 2,870.44.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks revived after buy-backs of bank shares resumed and a weaker yen encouraged investors seeking high-technology blue-chip issues. But trade was listless as there was little to steer the market apart from currencices. The 225-share Nikkei average ended the day up 135.65 points or 0.74 percent at 18,564.78.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed lower, pulled down by investors trimming overweight positions in bank shares. The Hang Seng Index closed 57.20 points lower at 13,450.08.

SYDNEY - Australian shares posted modest gains, the market's rise underpinned by solid gains from a handful of major resources issues boosted by firmer base metal prices. The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index closed 10.9 points firmer at 2,432.1.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares end sharply weaker on a stronger rand and a weaker bullion price which fell below the $360 per ounce level before the close. Industrials ended strong on less than convincing gains in Wall Street overnight. The overall index was down 21.2 points to 7,132.6, The gold index fell 70.0 points or 4.5 percent to 1,492.9, and the industrial index gained 22.7 points to 8,284.0.
